summary: Middle-aged man with HCV cirrhosis s/p TIPS, portal hypertension and multifocal metastatic hepatocellular carcinoma (left adrenal mets, no further oncologic options) transferred from an outside ICU after 10 days of intubation and vasopressor-dependent shock with Klebsiella aerogenes bacteremia. On arrival he had refractory distributive shock (warm, CVO2 80, three pressors, stress-dose steroids), lactate rising to 13.2, ARDS/hypoxic respiratory failure with large right pleural effusion, dialysis-dependent ATN, profound coagulopathy (INR 3.4, fibrinogen 77, platelets 44) concerning for DIC, rising transaminases (AST 2481) and bilirubin 13.3 indicating acute-on-chronic liver failure, plus unresponsive toxic-metabolic/hepatic encephalopathy. He continued to decompensate and died with family declining CPR and autopsy.
most_likely: Septic shock with Klebsiella aerogenes bacteremia complicating end-stage cirrhosis

differential.diagnosis: Septic shock due to Klebsiella aerogenes bacteremia
supporting_evidence: Transferred 'for septic shock', blood cultures grew Klebsiella aerogenes
Multi-pressor levophed/vasopressin plus third agent, stress-dose steroids
Lactate 6.6 → 13.2, pH 7.11, HCO3 7, anion gap 22
Warm extremities, CVO2 80 — distributive physiology
opposing_evidence: Cultures already treated 8 days with ceftriaxone; no new organism isolated here
Liver-failure vasodilation could mimic distributive shock
differential.reasoning: Documented organism-specific bacteremia with vasopressor-refractory distributive shock and severe lactic acidosis is the dominant reason for this stay and the likely principal coded disease.

differential.diagnosis: Acute on chronic hepatic failure in HCV cirrhosis with coma
supporting_evidence: AST 2481, ALT 439, total bilirubin 13.3, INR 3.4
Note: 'Acute on chronic Liver failure' with worsening HE
Cirrhotic nodular liver, TIPS, splenomegaly, ascites on RUQ US
Prior admissions for chronic hepatic failure and encephalopathy
opposing_evidence: Ischemic hepatitis from shock may explain much of transaminase surge
differential.reasoning: Marked hyperbilirubinemia, coagulopathy and unresponsive encephalopathy on a cirrhotic substrate meet acute-on-chronic liver failure; competes closely with sepsis as principal.

differential.diagnosis: Acute hypoxemic respiratory failure with ARDS requiring mechanical ventilation
supporting_evidence: Intubated for hypoxia, SpO2 50% at presentation; PEEP 14, FiO2 50%
CXR: worsening pulmonary edema, bilateral effusions right > left
Note documents ARDS, possible VAP, sputum with yeast
opposing_evidence: Volume overload and large pleural effusion also contribute
differential.reasoning: Ventilator-dependent hypoxemic failure with bilateral infiltrates is explicitly documented and a major comorbid complication of this admission.

differential.diagnosis: Acute kidney injury from acute tubular necrosis requiring CRRT
supporting_evidence: Creatinine 2.1–2.2 from baseline 0.6–0.8; K 6.5, HCO3 7
On CRRT, 22 L positive; HD lines both IJ
Attributed to septic shock and ATN without renal recovery
opposing_evidence: Hepatorenal physiology cannot be excluded in end-stage cirrhosis
differential.reasoning: Dialysis-dependent renal failure in the setting of shock is clearly documented and materially affected management.

differential.diagnosis: Disseminated intravascular coagulation with severe coagulopathy
supporting_evidence: Fibrinogen 77–95, INR 3.4, PTT 104, platelets 36–44
D-dimer 15335, haptoglobin <10, LDH 743
Bleeding from rectum, foley, and epistaxis; cryo/FFP/platelets given
opposing_evidence: Hepatic synthetic failure alone can produce identical coagulopathy
differential.reasoning: Consumptive picture with hypofibrinogenemia, very high D-dimer and multi-site bleeding supports DIC, though liver failure is a strong confounder.

differential.diagnosis: Metastatic hepatocellular carcinoma with adrenal metastases, terminal
supporting_evidence: Biopsy-proven left adrenal HCC metastasis; s/p RFA and failed chemotherapy
RUQ US: stable 2.6 cm hepatic lesion, large left adrenal mass
No further oncologic treatment available per referral center
opposing_evidence: Not the acute driver of this admission's decompensation
differential.reasoning: Active malignancy underlies the terminal trajectory and malignant effusion, and is a key comorbidity even if not the acute principal diagnosis.

supporting_evidence: RASS -5, no return of responsiveness off sedation
High gastric residuals, no bowel movements, lactulose not absorbed
Recurrent hepatic encephalopathy in both prior admissions
opposing_evidence: Sedation, uremia, and sepsis confound assessment; no ammonia level given
differential.reasoning: Persistent coma attributable to liver failure plus sepsis and uremia; multifactorial so scored below the organ-failure diagnoses.

differential.diagnosis: Atrial fibrillation/flutter with rapid ventricular response
supporting_evidence: History of a.fib/a.flutter s/p amiodarone bolus, now on metoprolol
Heart rate up to 103 recorded in ICU
opposing_evidence: Arose at outside hospital; no current rhythm strip or ECG documented here
differential.reasoning: Documented arrhythmia treated during the illness episode, but managed prior to transfer and not an acute issue in this stay.

supporting_evidence: Reported IVC thrombus at outside hospital, anticoagulation withheld
D-dimer markedly elevated; RV dilation with pulmonary hypertension on TTE
opposing_evidence: Current RUQ US: IVC patent, wall-to-wall flow; echoes felt artifactual
differential.reasoning: Reported historically but refuted by current imaging; retained as a low-probability differential for the RV dilation.

rule_outs.why: TTE showed hyperdynamic LV and warm extremities with CVO2 80; team judged cardiogenic cause unlikely.

rule_outs.diagnosis: Adrenal crisis from bilateral adrenal metastases
rule_outs.why: Considered given adrenal mets; empirically covered with stress-dose steroids without hemodynamic recovery.
Coffee-ground output raised concern; octreotide/PPI given, but no endoscopy or hemoglobin drop confirming active variceal bleed.
KUB showed no dilated loops or obstruction despite absent bowel movements.
Only small-volume ascites, no tap documented; blood source was Klebsiella bacteremia.

uncertain_areas: Whether a new resistant/ventilator-associated pneumonia or fungal infection was confirmed by final cultures
Ammonia level and degree to which encephalopathy was hepatic versus septic/uremic
